clue.text: Take a big risk with stage production using flames

parts.note: a play is a production put on in a theatre
taken as written
fire is what flames are

explanation.surface: A theatre director stages a show with real flames on stage, a dangerous gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to court danger recklessly, as one does when handling a blaze.

clue.text: Parcel from old servant contains even bits of oatcake

indicators.note: the servant word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a page was a boy servant in a great household

indicators.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word oatcake are taken

explanation.surface: A parcel arrives from a former retainer with crumbs of oatcake inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even bits of' picks the second, fourth and sixth letters of oatcake; 'contains' wraps the servant around them. A page was a boy servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are synonyms for something wrapped up for posting or delivery.

clue.text: American partners take a bit of inspiring

parts.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table
some means a certain amount, a bit

explanation.surface: A pair of Americans take a small share of something inspirational.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are North, South, East and West, with West and East playing as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fills you with wonder or admiration is awe-inspiring, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: Lakeland poet's semi-legend we hear, a master of language

indicators.note: semi means half, so the first half of the poet's name is kept

parts.note: William Wordsworth lived in and wrote about the Lake District

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a myth is a legend

explanation.surface: Half a legend about a Lake District poet is called a master of words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi' keeps WORDS, half of WORDSWORTH; 'we hear' turns MYTH into a sound-alike spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A person skilled with words, such as a gifted writer, is called by this term.

clue.text: High time rising upper class politician gets beat

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: U denotes upper class in British usage
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: It is high time a posh rising politician got a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns HT into TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat something is to hit it hard, a synonym of strike with a heavy blow.

clue.text: In favour of a Disney heroine endlessly following blueprint

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the heroine is dropped

parts.note: Mulan is the heroine of the Disney film of that name

explanation.surface: Someone backs a Disney heroine who follows a set plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' takes N from MULAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed plan or recipe for doing something, a synonym.

clue.text: Coloured arch made by artist's cool with nothing in black and white

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
in means fashionable or cool

indicators.note: in places the nothing letter inside the black and white pair

parts.note: B and W are abbreviations for black and white
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: An artist chills, with nothing in a black-and-white sketch, to make a coloured arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O between B and W.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is the arc of colours seen in the sky after rain, described literally here.

clue.text: Slyly keeping most of series for later

indicators.note: keeping means the first word holds the other inside

parts.note: subtly means slyly, in a cunning way

indicators.note: most of means the word for series is cut short at the end

parts.note: a sequence is a series

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly holds onto the bulk of a series for another time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last two letters of the series word here, not just one; 'keeping' has the sly word hold what remains after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning afterwards, at a following time.

clue.text: Obscure relative has ward but no wife or daughter

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: but no means the letters for wife and daughter are taken away

explanation.surface: An uncle has a ward but neither a wife nor a daughter, a murky family set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no' takes W and D from WARD, leaving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives mean not clear or hard to make out.

clue.text: British managed to acquire island with energy supplying land

parts.note: UK stands for the United Kingdom, so British

indicators.note: to acquire means the managed word takes in the island letter

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The British gained an island that supplies energy to the mainland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to acquire' puts I inside RAN, making RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a country, an example of a land or nation.

clue.text: Listener to lament on radio's lounging about first thing

parts.note: an ear is what one listens with

indicators.note: about means the lounging word goes around the other

parts.note: lying means lounging, reclining

indicators.note: on radio means the word is heard, not seen, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: to mourn is to lament

explanation.surface: A radio listener grieves on air while lazing about first thing in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' gives the sound-alike of the lament word, a poetic word for dawn; 'about' has the lounging word go around it.
explanation.definitionFit: First thing means at the very start of the day, a synonym phrase for dawn hours.

clue.text: Main man's best friends are old sailors

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea
the dog is called man's best friend

explanation.surface: The chief person's pet dogs turn out to be veteran mariners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, but it is the old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for experienced seamen who have spent years at sea.

clue.text: Tradesman's beginning to paint old furniture

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: lumber is old, discarded furniture stored away

explanation.surface: A tradesman starts painting some old furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use, lumber is junk furniture and other unwanted household items, not timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber, who fits pipes and drains, is an example of a tradesman.

clue.text: Verbal prompt gets people in line

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the prompt word is heard as a sound-alike

parts.note: a cue is a prompt given to an actor

explanation.surface: A spoken prompt gets a crowd to form a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people waiting their turn, at a bus stop for example, has this British name.

clue.text: Home and Away's tackling serious suffering

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: tackling means the away word grips the serious word

parts.note: away taken as written, with the 's read as is
bad means serious, as in a bad injury

explanation.surface: The soap opera Home and Away is taking on some heavy subject matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackling' has the away word grip the serious one. Home and Away is a long-running Australian TV soap, and the surface leans on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for being seriously unwell or in great distress.

clue.text: Fool's put up to trapping spies by English colleague

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: trapping means the reversed word holds the spies inside
put up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A fool is set up to catch spies with help from an English colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns the little word to round to OT; 'trapping' holds the American spy agency inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a partner or coworker, a synonym.

clue.text: They protect viewers with opinion getting attacks

parts.note: eye means judgement or view, as in to my eye
lashes out means attacks; lashes are verbal attacks

explanation.surface: Some critics with strong views launch attacks on the TV audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' looks like an audience, but it means the eyes themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The fringes of hair on the eyelids keep dust out of the eyes, which are viewers.

clue.text: Spandex is designed for stretches

indicators.note: designed means newly arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The stretchy fabric is made to give way as it is pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to grow larger or extend, as stretchy fabric does.

clue.text: Top class model expressed hesitation about couch in artist's studio

parts.note: A means first class, the top grade
the Model T was Ford's famous car

indicators.note: about means the hesitation sound goes around the couch word

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
to couch is to lie down, recline

explanation.surface: A top model hesitates over a couch in a painter's workroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Ford's famous car; 'about' wraps the hesitation sound around the reclining word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the French word for a workshop, used in English for a painter or designer's workspace.

clue.text: Joan Baez initially composed for a stringed instrument

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the singer's surname
composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Folk singer Joan Baez wrote a piece for a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives B from Baez, joined with JOAN for 'composed' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a plucked instrument with strings, an example of the type.

clue.text: Depressed about rights Germany's made vague

indicators.note: about means the depressed word goes around the rights

parts.note: blue means down or depressed
R is an abbreviation for right, so two make rights
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Germany's view on rights is fuzzy and gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the gloomy colour around two R's; D is Germany's international vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is made indistinct and unclear, it becomes fuzzy, a synonym.

clue.text: Etna's eruption engulfed four, young with a lack of experience

indicators.note: engulfed means the scrambled volcano letters swallow the four
eruption throws the letters into disorder

parts.note: Etna, the Sicilian volcano, taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The eruption of Etna engulfed four inexperienced youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eruption' rearranges the volcano's letters to NAET; 'engulfed' sets the Roman four inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means innocence or a lack of worldly knowledge, a synonym.

clue.text: Sets off to bring in work left uncovered

indicators.note: to bring in means the scrambled letters hold the others inside
off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A film crew sets off to bring in some work that is left exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SETS to TESS; 'to bring in' puts OPL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes being naked above the waist, a kind of being bare.

clue.text: Sweetheart used up pasta sauces

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: ragus are Italian meat sauces served with pasta

explanation.surface: A darling has finished off the pasta sauces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RAGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an affectionate form of address, like honey or darling.

clue.text: Warning when sale's about to go ahead

indicators.note: to go ahead means the letter moves forward to the front

parts.note: an auction is a sale
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A warning is given when a sale is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go ahead' moves the C in AUCTION to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean an advisory notice about danger.

clue.text: Pulling any trick's essentially legit to protect family

indicators.note: to protect means the other letters go around the family word
trick means deceive or twist, so the letters are rearranged
essentially means the central letter of the word

parts.note: kin is family

explanation.surface: Pulling any trick is fine, essentially legal, if it protects the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trick's' rearranges the word any to YAN; 'essentially' takes the centre of legit; 'to protect' has those letters surround the family word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanking is pulling suddenly and hard, a synonym.

clue.text: Reach consensus about a good time to bring in soldiers

indicators.note: to bring in means the other letters take in the soldiers

parts.note: an eon is a long period of time
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: People settle on a good time to call in the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring in' puts RE after AG, inside the run AGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle on something together is to come to an agreement over it, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Employer led in new cook described as easy to work with

parts.note: a user is one who employs something

indicators.note: described means drawn around, so the cook word goes around the others

parts.note: to fry is to cook

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An employer brings a new cook into the kitchen who is easy to get on with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the words led in to IENDL; 'described' has the cooking word drawn around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a gadget or system that is simple to operate.
